name: Arlington Memorial Bridge
note: Roadway is bike-legal end to end and one authority throughout; the midpoint heuristic must not split it. Checked against the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24: one highway=primary way of that name, two-way. Owner statements, 2026-09-26: "Mass ride can cross the Potomac at Chain Bridge, Key Bridge, and Memorial bridge without using a trail." And, of the roadway, after the same rule for Key Bridge ("I wouldn't route someone onto that outside of a mass ride."): "Same with memorial bridge." So roadway_mass_ride_only is true: the no-trail variant keeps the roadway for a mass ride and the standard and e-bike variants bar it (bicycle=no). They are not stranded: on the 2026-09-24 extract the bridge carries two highway=cycleway ways of its own name, one each side (50579250 and 69200708), bicycle=designated, foot=designated, bridge=yes, which is how an ordinary rider crosses. The roadway is the one bridge-tagged way of the name (468423958), stress tier 4 on the promoted build. The roadway lands a mass ride on Columbia Island, whose road exits in that extract are all motorway or motorway_link (the George Washington Memorial Parkway and its ramps, Washington Boulevard) or bicycle=no (North Boundary Drive, the Arlington National Cemetery drives), so a no-trail route across it reaches Memorial Circle and Memorial Avenue and nothing further into Virginia; that is OSM's tagging of the approaches, not this row. Owner decision, 2026-09-26, on that Virginia landing: "Turn at Memorial Circle". For a mass ride Memorial Bridge is an out-and-back from the District - across, around Memorial Circle, and back - with no onward route into Virginia, and no access change is made to the Columbia Island roads. Owner decision, 2026-09-26, asked whether a Group Ride with its "Allow bike paths and trails" switch off should be kept off the Key and Memorial Bridge roadways: "No, allow them" ("A trails-off Group Ride may use those bridge roadways like a mass ride."). Owner decision, 2026-09-26, asked what trails-off should do for ride types other than Mass Ride and Group Ride: "Every type, roadways ok" ("Offer trails-off on every ride type; like Group Ride, it may use the Key and Memorial roadways."). So the roadway is for any trails-off ride - every ride with trails off gets the no-trail variant (variants.variant_for) - and the standard and e-bike variants still bar it.

name: Key Bridge
note: The roadway is a legal, ordinary climb, not barred - riders use it every day. Until 2026-09-26 this row was sidepath_only, on the reasoning that a narrow bridge with no shoulder and no way off mid-span had to keep a mass ride to the sidewalk, which dropped the roadway from the no-trail variant and, with the sidewalk dropped as trail class, left a mass ride no crossing here at all; the owner reversed that (below). roadway_bicycle_legal is the legality claim; roadway_mass_ride_only is a routing rule, not a legal one. The DC-Virginia boundary on the Potomac is the 1791 Virginia shoreline, not the channel, so this span lies within the District along essentially its whole length and MPD's jurisdiction runs end to end - the same shape as the Arlington Memorial Bridge row, which is the right shape for every Potomac span. The earlier split down the middle was the midpoint heuristic written into the data. Boundary is a matter of record; the policing that follows from it is community working knowledge, not a legal statement. The Virginia approach ramps beyond the abutment are VDOT's and Arlington County's; the structure is not. Checked against the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24: inside this file's region the name reaches four highway=trunk ways, ref US 29, and nothing else; Baltimore's Francis Scott Key Bridge (I-695, the name in bridge:name) is the other structure of that name in the coverage area and is outside it. All four roadway ways carry bicycle=no and foot=no in that extract, so this row's roadway_bicycle_legal true is a claim against OSM's own tag, and the remap writes bicycle=yes over it. Owner decision, 2026-09-25: the claim stands against OSM's bicycle=no - the roadway is legal to ride, and roadway_bicycle_legal stays true. Owner statements, 2026-09-26: "Mass ride can cross the Potomac at Chain Bridge, Key Bridge, and Memorial bridge without using a trail." - so sidepath_only is false and the no-trail variant keeps the roadway; "Key bridge is sidepath perferred."; and, superseding that with a stronger rule, "I wouldn't route someone onto that outside of a mass ride." So roadway_mass_ride_only is true: the standard and e-bike variants bar the roadway (bicycle=no) and an ordinary rider crosses on the sidewalk, while the no-trail variant keeps the roadway for a mass ride (that variant is Mass Ride's layer 1, and PLAN also names it for Group Ride with trails off). On the 2026-09-24 extract the sidewalk is highway=footway, footway=sidewalk, bicycle=designated, bridge=yes, unnamed, so no name match can reach it (ways 38772020, 1430201496 and 50575692 among them), and the four roadway ways are stress tier 4 on the promoted build (mixed traffic, 30 mph, multilane). Owner decision, 2026-09-26, on the Virginia approaches, North Fort Myer Drive (way 50426889) and North Lynn Street (way 116044202), both US 29, highway=trunk, bicycle=no and foot=no in OSM and the only roads off the roadway's Virginia end: "Bikes are legal, but there's a side path that's a better option for most." That is an access correction, so it is carried by approved access overrides (fixtures/overrides/2026-09-26-owner-bicycle-access.json, loaded by manage.py load_access_overrides), not by this row; with them a mass ride uses the roadway end to end, and ordinary riders stay on the sidewalk because this row's roadway_mass_ride_only bars the roadway to them. Owner decision, 2026-09-26, asked whether a Group Ride with its "Allow bike paths and trails" switch off should be kept off the Key and Memorial Bridge roadways: "No, allow them" ("A trails-off Group Ride may use those bridge roadways like a mass ride."). Owner decision, 2026-09-26, asked what trails-off should do for ride types other than Mass Ride and Group Ride: "Every type, roadways ok" ("Offer trails-off on every ride type; like Group Ride, it may use the Key and Memorial roadways."). So the roadway is for any trails-off ride - every ride with trails off gets the no-trail variant (variants.variant_for) - and the standard and e-bike variants still bar it.

name: Chain Bridge
note: A standard, bike-legal climb out of Georgetown - not barred. sidepath_only is true: the no-trail variant drops the roadway, because Chain Bridge is not a mass-ride crossing (owner, 2026-09-26, below). It was set before that on a different reasoning - that with a five-foot sidewalk and no way off mid-span a mass ride could not use the roadway - which the owner's first statement of 2026-09-26 contradicts; the value stands for the owner's later answer, not for that reasoning. The DC-Virginia boundary on the Potomac is the 1791 Virginia shoreline, not the channel, so this span lies within the District along essentially its whole length and MPD's jurisdiction runs end to end - the same shape as the Arlington Memorial Bridge row, which is the right shape for every Potomac span. The earlier split down the middle was the midpoint heuristic written into the data. Boundary is a matter of record; the policing that follows from it is community working knowledge, not a legal statement. The row previously named Fairfax County Police for the Virginia end, which was wrong twice over: the Virginia abutment is in Arlington County, not Fairfax, and on the boundary above it is not a Virginia authority's to police at all. Checked against the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24: two highway=primary ways of that name, two-way, one of them carrying ref VA 123. Owner statements, 2026-09-26, in order. First: "Mass ride can cross the Potomac at Chain Bridge, Key Bridge, and Memorial bridge without using a trail." Then, asked about the District approach, Canal Road NW (ways 397297433, 469107787, 50773201; highway=trunk, bicycle=no in OSM): "No" - it stays barred. The other road off the roadway's District end, the Clara Barton Parkway (way 889043769, also highway=trunk, bicycle=no), was not part of that question; it stays as OSM tags it, and no owner answer is recorded for it. Then, asked whether Chain Bridge is a mass-ride crossing given Canal Road stays barred: "Not a mass-ride crossing". That last answer is what sidepath_only records. Leaving the roadway in the no-trail graph would not have made a crossing of it - it leads to nothing on the District side - but it did leave a dead-end spur: on a rebuilt no-trail graph of the 2026-09-24 extract, a no-trail route from North Glebe Road in Arlington to the District end of the bridge ran the whole 405 m of roadway way 26708895 and stopped at the abutment. Dropping the roadway removes that, and does not depend on how OSM tags Canal Road next year. The owner did not make this roadway mass-ride-only, so roadway_mass_ride_only is false and the standard and e-bike variants keep both the roadway and the footway named Chain Bridge (way 61433253, bicycle=yes), which is trail class and so is not in the no-trail graph either. For a mass ride, Key Bridge is the crossing into Virginia.

name: George Mason Memorial Bridge
note: One of the five parallel structures at the 14th Street crossing, which this file used to record as three. The five are three highway spans - Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial (1950), George Mason Memorial (1962), Rochambeau (1972) - plus the Long Bridge carrying freight and commuter rail and the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge carrying Metro's Yellow Line. Not one bridge and not one answer, which is why they are separate rows. This one carries I-395's southbound lanes out of the District, and it is where the shared-use path is: the Mount Vernon Trail connection that ramps to Columbia Island on the Virginia side and Ohio Drive SW on the District side is a sidewalk on this highway span, not a structure of its own and not on the Metro bridge. The roadway carries bicycle=no, so roadway_bicycle_legal is false; the path is the only and the intended crossing, so sidepath_only is true. Two claims here are community knowledge rather than record and they are not held at the same confidence. That this span is the one carrying the path is medium-high, from the reviewer who rides it, and it is the one claim a survey could move. The direction is medium-high too and was recorded backwards until round 5: the 1950 Williams span carries the northbound lanes into the District - it is the span Air Florida flight 90 struck - so this 1962 span carries the southbound lanes out of it. Names checked against the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24: two highway=motorway ways, ref I 395;US 1, bicycle=no, oneway and drawn from the District end toward Virginia, which agrees with the southbound direction above. Which span carries the path is not something that check can see.

name: Rochambeau Bridge
note: One of the five parallel structures at the 14th Street crossing, which this file used to record as three. The five are three highway spans - Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial (1950), George Mason Memorial (1962), Rochambeau (1972) - plus the Long Bridge carrying freight and commuter rail and the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge carrying Metro's Yellow Line. Not one bridge and not one answer, which is why they are separate rows. The 1972 span. This note said it carried the US-1 local lanes rather than the I-395 freeway lanes, and the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 has it the other way round: its two ways are highway=motorway, ref I 395 EXPR - the express lanes - one each way, with the name in bridge:name, while US 1 is on the Williams and George Mason spans (ref I 395;US 1). This note also said bicycle=no on the roadway; neither way carries a bicycle tag, and motorway class is what bars it. There is no sidepath on this structure, so it is barred outright rather than sidepath-only. Names checked against that extract; the authority columns remain community working knowledge.

name: Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial Bridge
osm_names: Arland D. Williams Junior Memorial Bridge
note: One of the five parallel structures at the 14th Street crossing, which this file used to record as three. The five are three highway spans - Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial (1950), George Mason Memorial (1962), Rochambeau (1972) - plus the Long Bridge carrying freight and commuter rail and the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge carrying Metro's Yellow Line. Not one bridge and not one answer, which is why they are separate rows. This row said this was the Metrorail bridge and that it carried the Mount Vernon Trail connection. It is neither. It is the 1950 highway span carrying I-395's northbound lanes into the District - the one Air Florida flight 90 struck in January 1982, renamed in 1985 for the passenger who passed the rescue line to others and drowned. That it is the 1950 span and that it is the span flight 90 struck are matters of record, not OSM questions; which direction it carries is community knowledge at medium-high confidence and was recorded backwards until round 5, as southbound. The Metro crossing is the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge, a separate structure with its own row, and the shared-use path is on the George Mason Memorial Bridge. So this span is bicycle=no on the roadway with no sidepath on it: barred outright, not sidepath-only. The OSM spelling writes Junior out - "Arland D. Williams Junior Memorial Bridge" - so the row matched nothing until osm_names said so. On the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 that name is on six highway=motorway ways, ref I 395;US 1, bicycle=no, oneway and drawn from the Virginia end toward the District, which agrees with the northbound direction above; the direction is still community knowledge that the map happens to agree with.

name: Charles R. Fenwick Bridge
note: One of the five parallel structures at the 14th Street crossing, which this file used to record as three. The five are three highway spans - Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial (1950), George Mason Memorial (1962), Rochambeau (1972) - plus the Long Bridge carrying freight and commuter rail and the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge carrying Metro's Yellow Line. Not one bridge and not one answer, which is why they are separate rows. This is the Metro crossing - the Yellow Line between Pentagon and L'Enfant Plaza - and it was missing from this file entirely while its name sat on the Williams row's note. A Metro bridge carries no roadway and no path: there is no bicycle access of any kind, which is why roadway_bicycle_legal is false and sidepath_only is false together. It is recorded so the structure has a row of its own rather than being rediscovered as somebody else's identity. The spelling is right and still cannot match: the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 carries "Charles R. Fenwick Bridge" in bridge:name on two railway=subway ways named Washington Metro - Yellow Line, and the pipeline reads highway ways only (extract.read_ways), so no rail way ever reaches the resolvers. The row reports itself unmatched on every rebuild for that reason rather than because the name is wrong, and osm_names_verified stays false because nothing the pipeline reads can confirm it.

name: Long Bridge
note: The fifth of the five structures at the 14th Street crossing, and the rail one: freight, and the commuter and intercity trains that share it. No roadway and no path. It has a row for exactly the reason the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge has one, and until round 5 it did not - this file stated a rule, "no row for anything rail-only", and then broke it for Fenwick one paragraph later. One rule for both: a structure at a crossing this deployment has an opinion about gets a row, whatever it carries, so that its identity is recorded here rather than rediscovered on somebody else's row. roadway_bicycle_legal and sidepath_only are false together, which is what "no bicycle access of any kind" looks like in these two columns. The name is the most collidable in this file - Arlington has a Long Bridge Park and a Long Bridge Drive - but the match is exact and restricted to bridge-tagged, non-trail-class ways, so a park path or a street named after the bridge is not reachable by it. Ownership is CSX's and row_owner_verified is false: the structure is CSX's, the trains on it are not all CSX's, and this file has not checked which entity holds the right-of-way at either abutment. Unmatched on the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 for two reasons at once: no way in it carries the name "Long Bridge", and the structure is rail, which the pipeline never reads (extract.read_ways keeps highway ways only). Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: Woodrow Wilson Bridge path
police: Alexandria PD / Prince George's County Police / MPD
note: The roadway carries I-95/I-495 and bicycle=no in OSM; the shared-use path is a separate structure and the only crossing. Three authorities, not two: the Maryland end is in Prince George's County, and the span clips the District itself - the Wilson Bridge is the one Potomac crossing that touches all three - so MPD belongs here alongside Alexandria and Prince George's. row_owner was MDTA and is now MDOT SHA: MDTA is Maryland's toll authority and this bridge is toll-free, which is the tell; MDOT SHA operates it. Medium confidence, and row_owner_verified stays false - ownership of the connecting right-of-way on the Virginia side (the Jones Point sliver, the short-crossing case) may sit with VDOT again. The name this row claimed, "Woodrow Wilson Memorial Bridge", is on no way in the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24, so the row matched nothing. There the roadway is twenty highway=motorway ways, ref I 95;I 495, bicycle=no: the western ways named "Capital Beltway (Local)" and "Capital Beltway (Thru)" with bridge:name "Woodrow Wilson Bridge" and "Woodrow Wilson Bridge (Thru)", the eastern ways named "Woodrow Wilson Memorial Bridge (Local)", some with bridge:name "Woodrow Wilson Memorial Bridge (Thru)". Those four spellings are what osm_names claims. The path is separate highway=cycleway ways named "Woodrow Wilson Bridge" and "Woodrow Wilson Bridge Trail"; the first shares a spelling with the roadway's bridge:name, and the trail-class guard is what keeps this row off it. Names checked against that extract.

name: Sousa Bridge (Pennsylvania Avenue SE)
note: Pennsylvania Avenue SE's Anacostia crossing, and one a mass ride can use: a bike-legal roadway, neither barred nor sidepath-only. The row's `name` is this file's own label, written to say which street the bridge carries; OSM's name is the full "John Philip Sousa Bridge", which is what `osm_names` now claims. Until round 5 the row carried no `osm_names` at all, so the label was what the resolver matched on - a string with a parenthesis in it that no OSM way carries, which could only ever miss, and a miss here is silent except in the unmatched log. Checked against the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24: the bridge:name is on the two highway=primary ways of Pennsylvania Avenue Southeast across the Anacostia, one each way. Owner statement, 2026-09-25: the District's Anacostia crossings accessible by bike are the Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge, the 11th Street local span, the Sousa Bridge on Pennsylvania Avenue and the Benning Road Bridge, and this is one of them; with the Whitney Young Memorial Bridge, also confirmed legal, that is every Anacostia crossing in this file whose roadway_bicycle_legal is true.

name: 11th Street Bridge (local span)
note: One of the three parallel structures at the 11th Street crossing, which this file used to record as one row. That row said in its note that the local span carries bikes and the freeway spans do not - two different answers to the two columns the pipeline reads, written where nothing reads them, with one set of values standing for all three structures. Split the way the 14th Street crossing is split and for the same reason: "may a bicycle use the 11th Street Bridge" has no single answer. The local span, carrying 11th Street SE between Capitol Hill and Anacostia. A bike-legal roadway with its own provision and a connection to the Anacostia Riverwalk Trail at either end, so it is neither barred nor sidepath-only: this is the row that makes the 11th Street crossing usable by a ride, and the one the old single row's values described. This row claimed the plain name "11th Street Bridge" as the local span's, and the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 has that name on exactly one way, which is not this span: bridge:name on way 546095934, highway=motorway, name Southeast Freeway, ref I 695 - a freeway span, where this row's true landed. The claim is removed. The candidates for the local span in that extract are four bridge ways named "11th Street Southeast", highway=secondary, one about 270 m long beside the freeway span and three short ones at its south end, and every one of them carries bicycle=no and foot=no. Claiming that name would put this row's true on all four, so the row is pinned by osm_way_id instead, to the one of them that crosses the river. Owner statement, 2026-09-25: it is legal to ride both the local span's roadway and the shared-use path on the south-west side of the spans, and the roadway is high traffic stress for a rider who does not take the path; of the three 11th Street spans, the south-westernmost is the ordinary roadway, the local span, and carries that path on its south-west side, and the other two are the I-695 freeway spans. The pin was chosen by geometry on the real extract (Geofabrik DC+MD+VA, 2026-09-24) and agrees with that statement: of the four ways, only 546096009 crosses the Anacostia (178 m of its 238 m over the river's water area, and across the waterway=river centreline); the other three are short ways south of the water. Its crossing of the centreline is the south-westernmost of the road spans, every I-695 way lying 35 to 65 m north-east of it. The path is way 546096004, highway=cycleway, Anacostia Riverwalk Trail, bicycle=designated and foot=designated with no access or vehicle restriction, about 12 m south-west of the roadway, which carries sidewalk:right=separate on that side; the row does not point at the path, whose own tags already make it routable. OSM tags the roadway bicycle=no and foot=no, and this row's true, confirmed by the owner, is what the remap writes bicycle=yes over. The stress point is a note only: the classifier derives stress from the way's tags. osm_names_verified stays false because the row claims no OSM name; the pin, not a name, is what was checked. Owner statement, 2026-09-25: the District's Anacostia crossings accessible by bike are the Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge, the 11th Street local span, the Sousa Bridge on Pennsylvania Avenue and the Benning Road Bridge, and this is one of them; with the Whitney Young Memorial Bridge, also confirmed legal, that is every Anacostia crossing in this file whose roadway_bicycle_legal is true. Owner decision, 2026-09-26, on the local span's south landing, the 11th Street SE ways 546095996, 546096006, 546095995 and 546095994 (highway=secondary, bicycle=no and foot=no in OSM): "Yes, legal for all". Bicycles are legal there in every variant; it is an access correction, so it is carried by approved access overrides (fixtures/overrides/2026-09-26-owner-bicycle-access.json, loaded by manage.py load_access_overrides) rather than by this row. Those four are not enough on their own, checked on a rebuilt no-trail graph of the 2026-09-24 extract: the landing continues south as three more 11th Street SE ways (546095992, 546095991, 546095993) and then Martin Luther King Jr Avenue SE (589551026, 371431399, 589551027), all bicycle=no and foot=no, before it meets a road a bicycle may use. With all ten opened the no-trail variant crosses the span both ways (1.45 km); with the four alone it still detours by the Sousa or Douglass bridge. Owner decision, 2026-09-26, on those six ways: "Legal for all. It might be discouraged as it's a very busy road". Legal for all per the owner, who added that it might be discouraged as it is a very busy road; that is not an access decision, and the six ways are opened by six more rows in the same override file. (Not the owner's words: this project's stress tier does not steer a Default route away from them today - it reaches the router only as a comfort tag on tier-1 ways, and stress-weighted ranking is not built. What steered ordinary rides off these ways until 2026-09-27 was the penalty below.) Owner decision, 2026-09-26, asked whether the planner should steer ordinary riders going south from the Navy Yard to Anacostia back to the Riverwalk once those rows are loaded: "Steer to the path" ("Keep it legal but add a penalty on that roadway for ordinary rides so the Riverwalk wins when it's close in length."). So ordinary_ride_penalty_way_ids names the roadway: this span (546096009) and the ten landing ways above. The standard and e-bike variants carry a penalty there (rm:ordinary_ride_penalty, which the transform writes as Valhalla's bicycle=use_sidepath: legal both ways, costlier, no change to speed); bicycle=use_sidepath is used only for its cost - its OSM meaning, a compulsory sidepath, is not claimed, and nothing user-facing may read it as one; the no-trail variant is unchanged. A penalty, not a bar: a route still takes the roadway where it is clearly shorter or the only way. Retired 2026-09-27 (the owner: "Retire it (Recommended)"): this row no longer carries ordinary_ride_penalty_way_ids; the span and the ten landing ways are curated LTS 4 (fixtures/overrides/2026-09-27-owner-stress.json; the owner: "11th street is LTS4"), whose stress penalty is the same bicycle=use_sidepath write, and the owner's "Steer to the path" is quoted in those rows.

That row said in its note that the local span carries bikes and the freeway spans do not - two different answers to the two columns the pipeline reads, written where nothing reads them, with one set of values standing for all three structures. Split the way the 14th Street crossing is split and for the same reason: "may a bicycle use the 11th Street Bridge" has no single answer. One of the two freeway spans, carrying I-695 inbound toward the Southeast Freeway. bicycle=no on the roadway and no sidepath on the structure, so it is barred outright rather than sidepath-only. The OSM spelling is the least confident claim in this file: freeway spans are frequently unnamed in OSM, and this is a guess at a plausible name, so the row may well land in the unmatched log - which is where a rule that is not biting is supposed to appear, and is why that log exists. That is tolerable here because I-695 is motorway class, which MOTOR_ONLY does catch, so a ride is kept off these two spans by highway class even when the name resolves against nothing. The one freeway way there named for the crossing is 546095934 - bridge:name "11th Street Bridge", name Southeast Freeway, ref I 695, oneway, drawn from the Anacostia end north-west toward the Southeast Freeway - and nothing here decides which of the two freeway rows it belongs to. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract. Owner statement, 2026-09-25: the 11th Street Bridges include a span on I-695 that restricts bicycles, which confirms this row's columns as they stand. Pinned by osm_way_id to 546095934 on the real extract (Geofabrik DC+MD+VA, 2026-09-24): of the freeway ways that cross the Anacostia's centreline, it is the only one drawn - and so, being oneway, travelled - north-west, toward the Southeast Freeway, and the whole inbound river span is that one way (182 m of its 193 m over the water; the two ways it splits into at the north bank carry under 10 m each). osm_names_verified stays false: the spelling above is still a guess and the pin, not the name, is what was checked.

name: Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge
note: South Capitol Street's Anacostia crossing; a bike-legal roadway with its own protected provision, not a sidepath-only case. Checked against the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24: the bridge:name is on the two highway=primary ways of South Capitol Street across the Anacostia, one each way. Both carry bicycle=use_sidepath, so this row's roadway_bicycle_legal true is a claim against OSM's own tag, and the remap writes bicycle=yes over it. Owner decision, 2026-09-25: the claim stands against OSM's bicycle=use_sidepath - the roadway is legal to ride, and roadway_bicycle_legal stays true. Owner statement, 2026-09-25: the District's Anacostia crossings accessible by bike are the Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge, the 11th Street local span, the Sousa Bridge on Pennsylvania Avenue and the Benning Road Bridge, and this is one of them; with the Whitney Young Memorial Bridge, also confirmed legal, that is every Anacostia crossing in this file whose roadway_bicycle_legal is true.

name: Whitney Young Memorial Bridge
note: A bike-legal roadway. Owner statement, 2026-09-25: the bridge, which carries East Capitol Street, is legal to ride and has a path; the owner had left it off the list of bike-accessible Anacostia crossings only because it connects to few good routes. That confirmation replaces the basis this row had, a reviewer's word that it belonged in this set. The Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 confirms the location and the spelling: three highway=primary ways named "Whitney Young Memorial Bridge" at East Capitol Street's crossing of the Anacostia, one of them bicycle=yes. The alias "Whitney M. Young Jr. Memorial Bridge" is removed from osm_names because no way in that extract carries it. The authority columns remain community working knowledge. The path, on the real extract of 2026-09-24, is two ways of its own, one on each side: highway=footway, footway=sidewalk, bicycle=yes, foot=yes, no access restriction - 694510343 on the north side, beside the westbound roadway, and 796356181 on the south side, beside the eastbound roadway, each about 7 m from it and crossing the river with it; the two roadway ways that carry sidewalk:right=separate point at them.

name: Theodore Roosevelt Bridge
note: Carries I-66 and US-50 across the Potomac, with no sidepath on the structure, so this is barred outright rather than sidepath-only. This note said the bridge was tagged highway=trunk, which MOTOR_ONLY does not catch, so that the no-trail variant depended entirely on the rm:bridge_bicycle mechanism to keep a mass ride off it; it also said bicycle=no in OSM. The Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 disproves both: OSM names the structure "Theodore Roosevelt Memorial Bridge" - which is why this row matched nothing until osm_names said so - and all seventeen of its bridge ways are highway=motorway, refs I 66, US 50 and I 66;US 50, with no bicycle tag at all. Highway class keeps a ride off it, and this row's false agrees with that rather than standing alone. Names checked against that extract; the authority columns remain community working knowledge.

name: American Legion Bridge
police: Montgomery County Police / Maryland State Police
note: Carries the Capital Beltway (I-495) across the Potomac near Cabin John. No bicycle or pedestrian provision of any kind - not sidepath-only, no access. The police column was a split down the middle, Montgomery County and Fairfax County, which is the midpoint heuristic this file exists to override, written into the data. The shoreline reasoning that puts every District span under one authority applies here with the line in a different place: above Washington the Potomac is Maryland's to the Virginia bank, which Virginia v. Maryland (2003) left undisturbed as to the boundary itself while deciding what Virginia may do from its own shore, so this span lies essentially in Maryland along its whole length. Montgomery County Police and the Maryland State Police, then, with Fairfax County reached only at the Virginia approach beyond the abutment - the same shape the Key Bridge row gives VDOT and Arlington County. Boundary is a matter of record; the policing that follows from it is community working knowledge at medium confidence, not a legal statement. row_owner reads MDOT SHA rather than "Maryland SHA", which is the same agency under a spelling this file no longer uses. The alias "George Kennan Memorial Bridge" has been removed: nothing places that name on this structure or on any other crossing in the coverage area, and an unplaceable alias in this file is a name that can only ever match the wrong way. Names checked against the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24: the bridge:name is on the two highway=motorway ways of the Capital Beltway, ref I 495, bicycle=no, one each way. The authority columns remain community working knowledge.
